headline: Hormuz sees 10 ships attacked in a week, the most since the war began; weighted funding rebounds from 3.80% to 9.20% while ETFs stay at −$856M over 7 days — leverage came back over the weekend, spot buyers did not.
summary: No ETF data over the weekend; price closed near the top of its daily range above the 50-day MA, but volume was only about 0.44× the 20-day average. Leverage shed the day before returned to 9.20%, and short-term holder SOPR dipped just below 1 at 0.9995. Market stage stays Bull (day 10); no exit rule has fired or is close. Next: whether Monday's ETF flows stop the bleeding, Hormuz and oil, and the Oct 27–28 FOMC.

By rule, Bull reverts to Bear only after 30 straight closes below a falling 200-day MA; days below now: 0. Tidemark low test: no break of 58,525 before 12/19.

news.title: UKMTO: at least 10 vessels attacked in or near the Strait of Hormuz since last Sunday, the most in a week since the war began in February, with 23 attacks in October; Iran's foreign minister says the seven-day plan stands — the strait reopens on day 6 if the US lifts its blockade and oil sanctions, talks on day 7
news.read: Strait risk is not easing; Brent settled at $109.86 on Friday, and high oil keeps inflation and hike expectations alive while the site's 10-year yield of 5.10% and real yield of 2.78% weigh on valuations. Iran's offer is conditional; Monday's oil reaction matters more. BTC edged higher on thin weekend volume — macro backdrop only, nowhere near the 200-day MA (−11.6%) or any exit condition.

news.title: US spot BTC ETFs lost about $228M net over 10/12–10/16 (Farside basis, author's sum): 10/13 +$175.7M, 10/14 −$261.4M, 10/16 −$82.4M; cumulative net inflows since launch about $56.9B
news.read: Matches the site's The Block figures day by day (10/16 preliminary). A second straight week of outflows: the seven complete days 10/07–10/15 total −$856.1M, and with a −0.133% Coinbase premium, US spot demand remains the weakest link; realized cap 30-day +1.33% is still positive — weak flows, not an exit condition.

news.title: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia continue: 6 injured in Najran on Sunday and Riyadh's Kingdom Centre moved to remote work after a drone alert; US VP Vance says Iran must sharply cut enrichment before the war ends — no breakthrough in talks
news.read: The conflict has spread from the strait to Saudi soil, keeping an energy risk premium in place and oil and yields elevated. For BTC this is a risk-appetite headwind transmitted mostly through equities and rates (30-day correlation with the Nasdaq 0.668); it does not change the market stage.

news.title: Strategy closed −9.6% at $136.83; its 8-K shows only 250 BTC bought 10/05–10/11 (avg $86,194) and about $192M of STRC preferred repurchased, with a 10/28 special meeting on STRC terms; MSCI's final list is due 11/11, effective at the 11/30 close
news.read: The largest listed holder is shifting cash toward buying back preferreds, with its smallest purchase of the year — another demand channel besides ETFs is slowing. A new 8-K usually lands Monday. No direct site metric; medium-term institutional backdrop, no change to the cycle view.

news.title: Market-wide liquidations about $315.2M over 24 hours, 66.3% longs; nearly $1B on 10/15, mostly longs
news.read: After the longs were cleared, the site's weighted funding went back from 3.80% to 9.20% over the weekend — leverage is returning faster than spot. With supply concentration at 14.88% (13.95% seven days ago), a move out of this zone tends to amplify volatility, but that says nothing about direction.

news.title: Nine US-listed companies, including Broadcom, CoreWeave and Verizon, objected to tokenized trading of their shares on OKXICE, the OKX–ICE venture; tokenized stocks totaled about $3.5B on 10/15, up from about $680M at the start of the year
news.read: Industry progress on merging crypto rails with traditional markets, with no direct link to BTC flows; no matching site metric, no change to any view.
